data.name: About_Description
data.value: Cyberdrome simulates an Android car radio with a virtual OBD port, so you can develop and test media, radio and OBD apps without a real car. It runs Android Automotive, emulates car models with their own themes, trouble codes, coding and GPS, and can also connect to a real OBD adapter.

data.name: About_Disclaimer
data.value: Cyberdrome comes without any warranty. It is a simulator for development and testing – not for use while driving. The car models' values, trouble codes and codings are made-up examples. Writing to real cars is at your own risk (the program is read-only by default). Android images with Google services are downloaded by you from Google and may only be used for development and testing. No manufacturer logos, fonts or security algorithms are included.

data.name: About_DonationText
data.value: Cyberdrome is free and open source. Development is funded by donations – every contribution helps with new car models, features and tests against real cars.

data.name: About_GplNotice
data.value: Cyberdrome © 2026 Jouko Broström. This program is free software: you can redistribute and modify it under the GNU General Public License version 3 or (at your option) any later version. It is distributed WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY. The program uses open source (including Avalonia, CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, Velopack, SQLite, SkiaSharp and .NET). Downloaded data: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), OBDb (CC BY-SA 4.0), Wikidata (CC0) and NHTSA vPIC. Everything is listed under Licence.

data.name: AndrObd_Help
data.value: How to connect AndrOBD to the virtual car: open AndrOBD → menu (⋮) → Settings → Connection type: Network (WiFi). Enter IP address 10.0.2.2 and port 35000. Go back and press Connect. Then choose e.g. OBD Data – speed and engine speed follow the sliders in Cyberdrome. AndrOBD is GPLv3 and is downloaded from F-Droid; it is not included with Cyberdrome.

data.name: Ui_WarningWritingCanChangeOrDamage

Every write shows a confirmation with control unit, service and data, and the original value is saved first in %AppData%\Cyberdrome\backup. Cyberdrome never computes manufacturers' security keys (UDS 27) – the key must come from the app. Turned off when the adapter is disconnected.
